answer.rationale: Compliance forbids reverting the security patch, so the rollback playbook in memory_b1 is unavailable. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fails fast and would shed settlement writes, which violates the no-lost-writes objective. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) previously helped by moving dashboard reads off the primary, not a write-heavy settlement peak. Regional failover (memory_b2) restored latency once, but failing over the write path at daily settlement peak risks consistency, duplicates, or lost customer writes. Adding capacity is the only remaining lever that can relieve write-path saturation without reverting the patch or dropping writes. memory_b3 supports headroom absorbing peak write load, but that add was done before the surge, so mid-incident effectiveness is uncertain—verify that record and apply as a standard experiment, not a fleet-wide change.
